provenance.distribution_packages: ports/fnv-nx/verify/env.json (cross packages g++-13-aarch64-linux-gnu, binutils-aarch64-linux-gnu, libc6-dev-arm64-cross, libstdc++-13-dev-arm64-cross, gcc-13-plugin-dev-aarch64-linux-gnu; versions are not copied)
provenance.runtime: README.md of the runtime external: binutils 2.45.1, gcc 15.2.0 + newlib 4.6.0.20260123 (devkitPro patches) + toolchain/msvcmodel/msvcmodel.patch, target aarch64-none-elf, multilibs ., pic, ilp32, ilp32/pic (the guest's libc, libm, libstdc++ and headers)

runtime_configure_cite.--disable-decimal-float: DATAMODEL.json (toolchain/msvcmodel) has no decimal-float row: the guest compiler offers no type the data model lacks, so the gcc configure of the guest compiler and its libgcc does not build the decimal-float runtime (libbid)
runtime_configure_cite.--disable-libstdcxx-pch: libstdc++-v3/acinclude.m4 GLIBCXX_ENABLE_PCH (GCC 13.3.0): --disable-libstdcxx-pch turns off attempts to use or build stdc++.h.gch; the guest has no precompiled header (the recipe compiles each unit hermetically from sources). Present in the devkitPro buildscripts' configure line this runtime follows (build-gcc-stage1.sh)
runtime_configure_cite.--disable-libstdcxx-verbose: libstdc++-v3/acinclude.m4 GLIBCXX_ENABLE_VERBOSE (GCC 13.3.0): --disable-libstdcxx-verbose turns off descriptive messages to standard error on termination (_GLIBCXX_VERBOSE=0). Present in the devkitPro buildscripts' configure line this runtime follows (build-gcc-stage1.sh)
runtime_configure_cite.--enable-libstdcxx-time=yes: the guest's declared machine has a monotonic clock, so chrono/this_thread take the POSIX clock path (acinclude.m4 GLIBCXX_ENABLE_LIBSTDCXX_TIME; its `auto` default has no arm for a `none` target and would leave steady_clock non-monotonic). The configure's own link tests (clock_gettime, nanosleep, sched_yield) are answered by rule CFG-LINK (runtime_configure_patch)

runtime_configure_patch.cite: libstdc++-v3/acinclude.m4 and config/no-executables.m4 GCC_NO_EXECUTABLES (GCC 13.3.0): with gcc_no_link=yes (set for a --with-newlib target so that autoconf's compiler-works step does not link) configure refuses every link test (the as_fn_error guard of AC_LINK_IFELSE, AC_CHECK_FUNC, AC_SEARCH_LIBS...); the guest runtime's objects reference the product link's protocol symbols, so a link test is answered by a static link (the linker's own archive closure, ld -r, over the driver's -### link line; leftover undefined symbols must be linker-script symbols of the ld default script or link/guest.ld, or protocol symbols the dispatch plugin declares): rule CFG-LINK, cfg_link.py
